methodology_name: BYS360 Canonical Quality / Readiness / Transferability Scoring Methodology
design_note: New canonical methodology, not a historical reconstruction. Legacy scores (Code Quality=68, Test Assurance=61, Security=70, CI/Release=79, Operations=64, Documentation/Handover=55, Maintainability=65, LIVE_READINESS=68, TRANSFERABILITY=61) are preserved as an unrelated historical snapshot in docs/governance/BYS360_SCORING_METHODOLOGY_V1.md and must never be used as calibration targets for this methodology's weights or formulas.

missing_evidence_policy.description: A gate or rubric signal that cannot currently be measured contributes 0 to its component (same numeric effect as a measured FAIL) and is never excluded from its denominator (excluding it would let unmeasurability inflate the score of everything else). Every such signal is recorded with status UNKNOWN (distinct from FAIL) in the calculator's trace output, and counted in a top-level unverified_evidence_count. The composite report exposes fully_verified=true only when unverified_evidence_count is 0 across all categories.
rejected_alternatives: neutral/50-point contribution: treats an unverified claim as half-credible, wrong default for a readiness score
silent exclusion from denominator: lets an agent inflate scores by making measurement unavailable
ceiling-only (no point deduction): too weak alone; the evidence-completeness ceiling below is a second, independent layer on top of this rule, not a replacement for it

double_counting_policy.description: Every CI/quality gate is assigned to exactly one category's gate_component. No gate command appears in more than one category's gates[] list. A debt-registry item's category field determines which single category's debt_penalty it affects; category is required to be a PRIMARY_CATEGORY per item, with no automatic secondary/global penalty.

canonical_python_note: All Python-based gate commands below invoke this exact interpreter explicitly (never a bare 'ruff'/'mypy'/'pytest' command). This is deliberate, not stylistic: this environment has been observed to have an unrelated, unpinned ruff/mypy on PATH from a different Python installation, which silently produces different findings than the project's pinned toolchain (ruff==0.16.0, mypy==2.3.0, per commit 27accc1). A methodology that relies on ambient PATH resolution is not reproducible across machines or even across shells on the same machine.

Maintainability.note: Deliberately has no ruff/mypy sub-metric to avoid double-counting with Code Quality, per double_counting_policy. Gated primarily on the absence of open P0/P1 debt anywhere (an unresolved P1 undermines whole-repo maintainability regardless of its assigned category) plus its own category's open-item count.

debt_penalty_policy.applies_to: status == OPEN items only, whose category field matches the scoring category (no cross-category penalty)
debt_penalty_policy.rationale: UNCLASSIFIED is deliberately non-zero (5, between P3's 3 and P2's 8) so leaving an item permanently unclassified is never a free way to avoid a penalty -- it must still be evaluated eventually. penalty_cap_per_category (30) prevents one category's debt from being wiped out by penalties alone; the composite-level evidence-completeness ceiling (below) provides the outer bound for missing-evidence risk, while measured (not missing) weakness is bounded by each category's own gate+rubric ceiling (max 100 before penalty).

evidence_completeness_ceiling.applies_when: any category feeding the composite has an UNKNOWN gate or rubric signal, OR registry.reconciliation_status != 'FULLY_RECONCILED'
evidence_completeness_ceiling.applies_to: LIVE_READINESS and TRANSFERABILITY composites only, not individual category scores
evidence_completeness_ceiling.rationale: A confidence gate on the composite, not a per-category penalty: it caps the headline number when the underlying evidence set is incomplete, without artificially suppressing a category that happens to be fully and honestly measured. It does NOT substitute for each category's own gate/rubric/penalty math correctly scoring a fully-measured-but-weak category below 89 already -- see docs/governance/BYS360_SCORING_METHODOLOGY_V1.md worked examples.

LIVE_READINESS.description: Production-readiness relevance weighting: how much would a failure in this category hurt if this code ran in production today.

TRANSFERABILITY.description: New-maintainer-onboarding relevance weighting: how much this category determines whether someone unfamiliar with the codebase can safely take it over.

implemented_in_v1: Coverage rubric uses coverage_ratchet's own combined_pct (line+branch), materially harder to inflate with tautological line-only tests than a line-only metric.
Handover doc substance is gated by the pre-existing tests/test_score100_handover_docs_contract_v1.py character-floor contract, not merely file existence.
UNCLASSIFIED debt items cost 5 points (not 0), so leaving items permanently unclassified is not a free scoring strategy.
Gate lists are literal, versioned commands (not prose), so two independent runs of the calculator against the same commit must produce the same category scores.
known_v1_gaps_deferred_to_v2: Suppression-comment counting (# noqa, # type: ignore deltas) is not yet a tracked sub-metric; a finding could in principle be silenced rather than fixed without this methodology detecting it.

broad_except count (used inside ops_audit/quality9) is except-block-count based, not statement-count based; merging many small except blocks into one large one could reduce the count without reducing actual defensive-coding sloppiness.
No independent AST-based same-name-multiple-definition detector; duplicate-code detection currently relies on the debt registry being manually kept current, not on automated re-discovery.
